transcript: The other night, I saw Breaking The Story at Second Stage. This new one act play by Alexis Scheer is about a war correspondent named Marina who has had her share of traumatic experiences reporting at the front lines of countless dangerous situations. She's come home to Massachusetts to accept a prestigious award, kindle a romantic flame and reconnect with her loved ones. But it's not so easy to leave everything that she's experienced behind her as she's constantly plagued by war flashbacks and PTSD induced nightmares. Though this play certainly covers some serious themes and debates heady topics like journalistic responsibility, it's also very funny. I actually thought the writing was at its sharpest and most captivating in its funny moments rather than the serious ones but overall the tonal balance of this piece feels pretty good. Based on the premise, I enjoyed the play more than I expected to and now I really wish I had seen our Dear Dead Drug Lord, also by Alexis Scheer, which Second Stage produced a few years back. Breaking The Story is running through June 23rd at the Tony Kiser Theatre. With that, another program for my collection.
